links.targetTitle: Removing the Core Facilitator requires two independent roles
Pattern's Agent-level and ecosystem-level emergency response
No adjudication process exists for misalignment by Ecosystem

title: Emergency preparedness failure removes an Ecosystem Actor from the group but derecognizes an Alignment Conserver entirely
content:
Two sibling documents set accountability for the same failure — deficient emergency preparedness — with identical process and radically different stakes.

Both open the same way: participation "is as critical to their overall performance evaluation as their customary deliverables," Core GovOps and the Protocol Security Workstream Lead "are required to document all instances" of failure, they hold discretion to evaluate deficiencies "given their domain expertise and proximity to each emergency situation," and neither "may proceed with removal unless it is supported with clear documentation."

The consequences then split. For an **Ecosystem Actor** (A.1.9.1.6.1), the remedy is escalating removal from the group: a deficient individual is removed; a deficient team member is removed; and "if different Emergency Response Group Members from the same Ecosystem Actor team consistently fail to meet requirements, the Ecosystem Actor team as a whole should be removed from the Group." Their underlying role survives — the removal is "incorporated into the evaluation of the Ecosystem Actor's overall performance."

For an **Alignment Conserver** (A.1.9.1.6.2), "that Member should be **derecognized** pursuant to A.1.5.9." Not removed from the ERG — removed from the ecosystem's AC track entirely, permanently and cross-role (A.1.5.10).

The escalation ladder for teams is well-designed: it distinguishes an individual's failure from a systemic one, and only condemns the organization once *different* members fail repeatedly. But the AC branch has no ladder at all. The same missed page that costs an Ecosystem Actor a seat costs an Aligned Delegate their delegateship.

This is the pattern noted elsewhere in the Governance Scope — enforcement severity tracks role category rather than conduct or discretion held. Both provisions also leave publication to discretion: whether supporting documentation is "retained internally or publicly shared on the Forum (with redactions, if needed)" is the decider's choice.
description: A.1.9.1.6.1 and .2 apply identical documentation and discretion rules to both populations, then diverge sharply on consequence — group removal versus loss of the underlying role.
